title: Companies Act, 2013 — Section 277 (Intimation to company liquidator, provisional liquidator and Registrar)

content.overview: The Tribunal causes the winding-up order to be intimated to the company liquidator and the Registrar, and the Registrar notes it on the register.
content.glance: The Tribunal causes the winding-up order to be intimated to the company liquidator and the Registrar, and the Registrar notes it on the register.
content.study: Companies Act, 2013 — Section 277 (Intimation to company liquidator, provisional liquidator and Registrar). The Tribunal causes the winding-up order to be intimated to the company liquidator and the Registrar, and the Registrar notes it on the register. Apply only the conditions, approvals, filings and penalties stated in the section. A rule made under the Act cannot contradict the section. Not a verified closure.

sections.heading: Rule
sections.body: The Tribunal causes the winding-up order to be intimated to the company liquidator and the Registrar, and the Registrar notes it on the register.

sections.heading: Explanation
sections.body: The order is also forwarded as the section requires. The intimation starts the liquidator's duty to take custody. It is not itself service on creditors.
